concepts.why: The patient presented with vision loss, tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and a mid-dilated pupil with a relative afferent pupillary defect, which are all consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma.
The patient experienced pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of his right eyelids and forearm, and had a significantly elevated creatine kinase level, which are indicative of rhabdomyolysis.
The patient had an elevated creatinine level, which suggests acute renal injury.
The patient presented with vision loss and a relative afferent pupillary defect, which are consistent with optic neuritis.
The patient presented with sudden vision loss and a mid-dilated pupil, which are consistent with central retinal artery occlusion.
The patient had a serous retinal detachment, which was evident on ophthalmoscopic examination.
The patient had a history of heavy alcohol consumption and presented with muscle pain, numbness, and elevated creatine kinase levels, which are consistent with alcoholic rhabdomyolysis.
The patient took buprenorphine and presented with muscle pain, numbness, and elevated creatine kinase levels, which are consistent with buprenorphine-induced rhabdomyolysis.

rationales.F01: Vision loss in one eye suggests a localized problem, such as acute angle-closure glaucoma or central retinal artery occlusion.
rationales.F03: Heavy alcohol consumption is a risk factor for rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F04: Buprenorphine can cause rhabdomyolysis, especially in high doses or with prolonged use.
rationales.F06: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm suggest a systemic condition, such as rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F07: No light perception in one eye indicates severe vision loss, consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma or central retinal artery occlusion.
rationales.F08: Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze are signs of acute angle-closure glaucoma.
rationales.F09: A mid-dilated pupil with a relative afferent pupillary defect suggests optic nerve damage, consistent with acute angle-closure glaucoma or central retinal artery occlusion.
rationales.F10: Elevated intraocular pressure is a hallmark of acute angle-closure glaucoma.
rationales.F11: Elevated creatinine levels suggest kidney damage, which can be caused by rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F12: Extremely high creatine kinase levels are diagnostic of rhabdomyolysis.
